_about: Every value the app uses, mapped to the Authority System Suite term that defines it (file relative to the suite's root, as the Authority Suite SDK bundles it). match: same = the suite defines this meaning; close = the suite has a nearby idea with a different boundary; none = the suite does not define it. Meanings read and checked against onysnow/Authority-System-Suite@b1c71e8 on 2026-10-11; the SDK now bundles d2b2186, against which tests/test_suite_map.py confirms each term is still present but the meanings have not been re-read. app/ai/suite_map.py serves it; tests/test_suite_map.py fails when a term here leaves the suite or an app value is not here.

mappings.note: A suite hypothesis must list supporting, contradicting and missing evidence and falsifiers; an app lead is an idea to check. The suite would need a bare 'lead' state with no evidence requirements (Policy §3 uses 'leads' only as a use of Tier D-F sources).

A Module 02 verdict listed by name only; the nearest classification, §4.4 Allegation, also needs who said it, when, and whether first-hand. The suite would need one claim-status term for 'stated, not yet checked'.
Module 02 lists VERIFIED without defining it; the TAS Claim record has no status field. The suite would need to define 'supported' for case claims.

Nearly the same meaning, but the suite counts only Tier D and above (never C), keeps testimony an allegation, and limits Tier A to propositions of its kind; the app checks independence of origin without tiers.
The suite applies it only after the §12 same-proposition test and only while the record cannot settle it; the app's 'evidence conflicts' has no such test.

mappings.suite_term: REFUTED (TAS- or RAS-tier evidence shows the premise false
mappings.note: Defined for LAS premises, not TAS claims; TAS Module 02 CONTRADICTED is listed but undefined. TAS would need a 'shown false' (ruled out) claim state.
Claim record field; the suite also wants the claim's warrant.
Claim record field.
The suite's context is a layer of sources that must never fill evidentiary gaps, not a per-link stance; the Claim record has no context list. The suite would need a third Claim-record evidence list.
The TAS Relationship record has only evidence_ids and an evidence_status (direct, inferred, alleged); the suite would need supporting and contradicting lists on it.
On Claim and Hypothesis records, not on the Relationship record.
A source layer, not a per-link review state.
§7.3 defines superseded as a document state, not a reviewer's verdict on an evidence link; the suite would need a link-level 'replaced by a later record' naming the replacing record.

TAS §7.3 makes superseded a document state and RAS Module 07 a research source's currency_status (SUPERSEDED), neither naming the record that replaces it. The app marks one claim's link to a record superseded, with the replacing record and a reason, and stops counting it for or against that claim (RAS Module 07 rules 4 and 5, read across). The suite would need a superseded_by on the evidence of the TAS Claim record.
A Module 06 conflict type; the app's value means 'reviewer has not decided', which the suite does not define for evidence links.
Webpage is narrower than web; EGS uses ONLINE / ONLINE_CAPTURE for gathering.
An EGS plan-item type; TAS source_type has no generic 'document' (it has email, filing, image...). TAS would need 'document' or a mapping to its kinds.
Testimony is the TAS source type; EGS treats an interview as a gathering route whose claims are uncorroborated.
Filing is narrower than public record; Tier A is a tier, not a type. TAS would need a public-record source type.
Social posts appear only as Tier F (leads only), an authority tier; TAS source_type has no social value.
The last value of the TAS evidence source_type list.
The suite calls every such pattern an investigative indicator that may justify inquiry, with no strength grading.
No graded red-flag strength exists in the suite (only Standard §10.2 'Red flags versus conclusions'). The suite would need a strength scale that still stops short of a finding.

The suite has no 'meets the published definition' level and leans against one (§10.2: patterns do not establish fraud). It would need a rule that meeting a published indicator definition is still an indicator, not a finding.
The suite has no record for a person's answer to whether a passage shows an indicator (Module 06 rule 1's evidence buckets are for hypotheses). It would need an indicator-check record.
As for 'shows': no indicator-check record.
As for 'shows': no indicator-check record.
A GAP- record needs much more than 'made a lead': what it bears on, why it matters, record existence, custodian, lawful route, priority.
UNKNOWN means 'the current record does not establish', not 'cannot be known'; the suite has no 'unknowable' for a missing value.
The suite's null rules do not separate not-applicable from unknown; it would need a not-applicable marker.
The suite keeps date precision and evidence status apart; the app mixes them in one field.
A claim verdict, undefined, not date-specific; the Event record's status has no defined list.
A date_precision value that needs the supported range and basis; the suite also has before, after and range.
The suite records a Conflict record, not an event status.
A classification, not an event-date status.
Bellingcat 'confirmed' has no tier floor or Tier A condition.
A likelihood term, not an evidence grade; the suite keeps likelihood apart from confidence.
Nearest is confidence LOW; the suite has no 'weak' grade.
A source says it but nothing corroborates it; Bellingcat's word is broader.
The record does not establish it.
TAS confidence LOW; IPCC's evidence axis (type, amount, quality, consistency) has a different boundary.
TAS confidence MEDIUM, as above.
TAS confidence HIGH, as above.
RAS degree of consensus is about a research community; TAS has no agreement axis for case sources.
RAS only.
RAS only.
The suite forbids a bare number in place of a likelihood term (CALIBRATED_CONFIDENCE_LANGUAGE Rule 1); a claim carries confidence_term, confidence LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH and confidence_basis.
The Entity record carries identity_confidence and identity_basis, not a decision.
A possible duplicate kept apart; no definitive 'not our party' state.
Kept apart pending evidence; no explicit 'unsure'.
Undefined Module 02 verdict; no 'accepted outside value' state.
A conflict type, applied after the same-proposition test.
Temporal change says both were true at different times; 'outdated' is not separately defined.
RAS currency status for research sources only.
Module 06 conflict type for a conflict the record does not settle.
The suite resolves a conflict only with named resolving evidence and forbids choosing the more convenient account.
A document state, not a conflict resolution.
Module 06 conflict type.
The suite splits 'both valid' into SCOPE DIFFERENCE and DEFINITIONAL MISMATCH; the app should name which.
Module 06 conflict type.
EGS PLANNED means written into the evidence plan, not 'not yet looked at'.
EGS: being sought.
EGS STOPPED needs a reason; no resumable 'blocked' state.
EGS DONE tracks work only; the outcome (obtained, refused, not held, no reply, unable to obtain) is a separate field the app lacks.
EGS NOT_SOUGHT needs a reason.
EGS needs a one-line reason with each priority.
The suite calls it 'medium'.
Same term; a reason is required.
No level above high; time sensitivity is a prioritisation factor (TAS Module 07 rule 2), not a level.
The ladder for the project's own trail records (a session may never record its own work above ALLEGED), not case work.
Names who confirmed and when; the app's 'accepted' should record who accepted it.
A trail-record re-check that did not hold.

mappings.suite_term: Every derived record must retain one or more evidence IDs
mappings.note: The suite also requires a warrant, not only linked items.

mappings.suite_term: Keep direct quotations exact and short
mappings.note: Module 02 rule 10 also needs the passage to support the exact proposition (scope, period, qualifiers), which a word-for-word match does not show.
The suite accepts an evidence ID, file plus location, a stable record ID, or a canonical URL with retrieval date.
The suite records the hash but has no rule to re-check it before marking a claim.

mappings.suite_term: a claim resting on it is classified UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT
mappings.note: The suite does not accept a written answer: the claim stays UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT until a resolution names resolving evidence.

mappings.suite_term: E and F remain leads only
mappings.note: The suite is tier-based (floor D, C never counts); the app uses source type as a stand-in because it records no tier.

mappings.suite_term: multiple independent reliable sources, or by one Tier A source
mappings.note: The suite adds the tier floor, excludes Tier C, keeps testimony an allegation, and collapses restatements.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Source tier A–F on each source or evidence record
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: source_tier_floor reads it to decide what may count toward a corroborated fact; without it the Confirmed and leads-only rules use source type as a stand-in.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Claim classification (one of the eight, Source statement … Unresolved conflict)
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: The suite's core label; the app's status cannot say whether a claim is an allegation, an inference or a negative search result.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Likelihood term per claim (the seven ICD 203 terms)
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Carried when a claim crosses to another system; a 0–1 number is not accepted in its place.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Confidence basis per claim
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: A stated reason for the likelihood term and the confidence level.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Warrant per claim
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Why the cited evidence bears on this claim (Module 08 rule 2).

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Assumptions per claim
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Inferences must state their assumptions (Standard §4.5).

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Limitations on claims and evidence
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: OCR, truncation, timezone and similar limits travel with the record.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Restatement link between evidence items
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Forwards and republications count as one source; without it independence cannot be judged as the suite defines it.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Authenticity status per evidence item
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Existence, authenticity and truth are kept apart (Module 02 rule 4).

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Issuer or author of the evidence
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Needed to judge first-hand knowledge, incentives and independence.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Separate record, event, publication and retrieval dates on evidence
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Standard §8 keeps them apart; the app stores one captured-on date.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Right-of-reply record and its status
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Checkpoint CP-01; a finding that accuses someone with no record is a blocking defect before publication.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Gap record
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: An unresolved question tied to a claim, with the record needed, whether it is known to exist, custodian, lawful route and priority.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Hypothesis records with the required alternatives
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Every consequential attribution needs at least one plausible alternative; the app holds hypotheses only in AI drafts.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Conflict record with the same-proposition test
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Disputed, conflicting and superseded decisions need the test and a resolution naming resolving evidence.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Retrieval log for material searches
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Without it a negative search result cannot be stated.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Negative search result as its own record
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: 'Not found' carries its search scope and never implies nonexistence.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Relationship evidence status: direct, inferred or alleged
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Each link says whether it is documented, inferred or alleged; the app records only for, against or context.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Event date precision and date type
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Precision (exact, day, month, range, before, after, estimated, unknown) is kept apart from evidence status.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Partly verified verdict with corrected wording
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: A partly supported claim needs wording that does not exceed the evidence.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Reviewer type on review events
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Tells an AI-assisted acceptance from a person's.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Source-protection record for confidential sources
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Required before contacting, storing or publishing anything about a confidential source.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Public-interest and proportionality record before publication
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: Dated before publication; the decision is a named person's.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Gathering outcome per lead (obtained, refused, not held, no reply, unable to obtain)
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: What was not obtained is a finding; 'resolved' does not say which.

suite_requires_app_lacks.what: Hash and custody log for online captures
suite_requires_app_lacks.why: No online item is relied on until its capture record exists.
